F-5-1: 5+ years in Korea on D-7 to E-7 (D-10 included) or F-2, age 19+; household income of 2× GNI or net assets of 1.5× the national household average; KIIP level 5 or the PR integration test (60+). If you apply while on E-7 or D-10: a bachelor's degree and a job.
F-5-2: 2+ years in Korea as the spouse of a Korean citizen (F-6): still married, raising your child together, or after a marriage that ended through no fault of yours. Household income of 1× GNI or household assets at the national median (80% when raising a child, pregnant, in infertility treatment, supporting your spouse's parents, or 60+); KIIP level 5 or the PR integration test.
F-5-3: Minor child of a Korean citizen with 2+ years on F-2-2, still under 19 when applying; no income test; KIIP level 5 or the integration test, unless you attend or finished regular Korean school.
F-5-4: Spouse or minor child of a permanent resident after 2+ years in Korea on F-2-3 (the F-5 holder needs no waiting period); household income of 1× GNI or assets; KIIP level 5 or the integration test (not for children under 15 or in Korean school).
F-5-6: 2+ years on F-4. Household income of 1× GNI with at least half of it your own (lower with KIIP 5, a Korean school or degree, or 100+ hours of volunteering), or another route: own net assets at the national household average, ₩500K+ of property tax last year, a pension from abroad of 1× GNI at 60+, ₩2bn of trade with Korea, US$500K invested, or a recommendation as a community leader. No KIIP needed.
F-5-6R: Regional overseas Korean (F-4-R) who has lived in the recommended depopulating area for 4+ years (2 years for those who were already there): household income of 70% of GNI instead of the full F-5-6 bar. Immigration handles it as F-5-6.
F-5-7: Ethnic Korean who already meets the requirements for Korean naturalization or nationality restoration; for the general and simplified naturalization routes also KIIP level 5 or the integration test.
F-5-9: Foreign doctorate in a high-tech field and regular employment in that field at a Korean company when you apply; income of 1× GNI or assets; no KIIP needed.
F-5-10: A high-tech bachelor's, a Korean STEM bachelor's, a Korean master's or a listed licence; 3+ years of residence in Korea and 1+ year of regular work at a Korean company; your own wage of 1× GNI; KIIP level 5 or the integration test.
F-5-13: Age 60+ with your own pension from abroad of at least 2× GNI a year (no asset route); no KIIP needed.
F-5-14: 4+ years with the same employer in manufacturing, farming, fishing, care or domestic work on H-2 (years after changing to F-4 count, and a forced move within 3 months to the same industry doesn't break them); a listed licence or your own income of 70% of GNI.
F-5-15: Doctorate from a Korean university's regular program and regular employment at a Korean company when you apply; income of 1× GNI or assets; no KIIP needed.
F-5-16: 3+ years on a points-based F-2 (F-2-7, F-2-7S or F-2-T); your own income of 2× GNI (family income doesn't count) or net assets of 1.5× the national household average; KIIP level 5 or the PR integration test.
F-5-18: Spouse or minor child of an F-5-16 holder after 2+ years on F-2-71; household income of 1× GNI or assets; KIIP level 5 or the integration test (not for children under 15 or in Korean school).
F-5-19: Spouse or unmarried child of the tourism/resort investor, granted together with the investor once the investment has been kept for 5 years; no income or KIIP test.
F-5-25: ₩3bn deposited in a designated public fund with a pledge to keep it for 5 years (withdrawing it cancels the status); covers your spouse and unmarried children; no income test, KIIP or residence period.
F-5-26: 3+ years as essential R&D staff of a foreign-invested company (D-8-1) with a bachelor's degree; household income of 2× GNI or net assets of 1.5× the national household average.
F-5-27: 2+ years as a recognised refugee (F-2-4); household income of 1× GNI or household assets at the national median; KIIP level 5 or the integration test.
F-5-28: 2+ years on F-2-16; household income of 1× GNI or assets; KIIP level 5 or the integration test.
F-5-29: Spouse or minor child of an F-5-28 holder; household income of 1× GNI or assets; KIIP level 5 or the integration test (not for children under 15 or in Korean school).
F-5-S2: Spouse or minor child of an F-5-S1 holder after 2+ years on F-2-71; household income of 1× GNI or assets; KIIP level 5 or the integration test (not for children under 15 or in Korean school).
F-5-T: 3+ years on F-2-T in a high-tech or science field; your own income of 3× GNI; KIIP level 3 or TOPIK 3.
F-5-T1: Spouse or minor child of a Top-Tier holder: permanent residence after 3 years on F-2-T1; no income or KIIP test.
F-2-99: 5+ years in a row on D-1, D-5 to D-9, E-1 to E-5, E-6-1, E-6-3, E-7 or F-1 (E-9 and student years don't count); your own income of ₩40M+ last year and ₩20M+ of your own financial assets held for 6+ months; KIIP level 4 or a Korean school or university diploma.
F-2-R: Local-government recommendation; a Korean associate degree or higher, or your own income of at least the recommending region's living wage; KIIP 3 or TOPIK 3; and a commitment to live, work or run a business in that depopulating area for 5 years.
F-2-T: World-class talent: a master's or PhD from a world top-100 university plus 8+ years of experience (3+ at a global top-500 company) or 5+ years of post-doctoral research; income of 3× GNI (4× GNI if you miss the degree or the career criterion); a ministry recommendation; KIIP 1 or TOPIK 1. As a change in Korea after 1+ year in a high-tech job: 2× GNI.
F-2-3: Spouse or minor child of a permanent resident (F-5). For a spouse, the F-5 holder's household needs income of 1× GNI (70% for 3 people or fewer; not needed with a child together or a pregnancy); no income test for a minor child.
F-2-71: Spouse or minor child of an F-2-7 holder who earns at least 1× GNI (otherwise the family gets F-1); no income test for the family of an F-2-7S holder.
F-2-7: 80+ points (age, education, Korean, income) on one of the tracks: 3+ years on a professional status (waived with income of ₩40M+), a Korean master's or higher with a job, a professional job at a listed company, or a job in a promising industry paying 1.5× GNI.
F-6-1: Legal marriage to a Korean citizen and a real home together. The Korean spouse's household needs income of 50% of the national median income (about ₩25.2M a year for 2 people in 2026, more for a bigger household; 5% of savings and property counts); not needed with a child together. You need basic Korean (TOPIK 1) or a shared language.
E-7-4: 4+ years on E-9, E-10 or H-2 in the last 10 years, TOPIK 2 or KIIP 2, an employer recommendation, 200/300 points and a contract of 2+ years at ₩26M+ a year; granted inside Korea only.
